code: nul_terminated_data = (unsigned char *) g_strndup ((const gchar *) data, size);
note: The fuzz input byte 0xfd is copied into a newly allocated string with only an added NUL terminator; the invalid incomplete UTF-8 byte is preserved.
The NUL-terminated but invalid UTF-8 string is passed directly into the date parser.
The parser proceeds with attacker-controlled str without first validating that it is valid UTF-8.
The same invalid string is forwarded into the token filling helper used by date parsing.
The single invalid byte contains no ASCII digits, so pt->num_ints remains below 3 and month-name matching is attempted.
The invalid NUL-terminated UTF-8 string is sent to UTF-8 case folding with length -1, which assumes well-formed UTF-8 and reads past the one-byte heap buffer while decoding the incomplete sequence.
The UTF-8 decoder reads continuation bytes for the leading 0xfd byte, crossing the heap allocation boundary.
